newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Six Bahrainis convicted on illegal leaflets charge.
newsitem.headline: Six Bahrainis convicted on illegal leaflets charge.

text.p: A Bahraini court on Saturday convicted six Shi'ite Moslems of possessing unlawful leaflets, but said the men should be set free because they had already spent 14 months in jail, a lawyer said.
"The court found them guilty but (found) that the period they had spent in jail was enough," the lawyer told Reuters. The six defendants were also fined 200 dinars ($531) each, he said.
The six Bahrainis -- imprisoned since their arrest in April 1996 -- are Hassan Qassab, Shaker al-Mahouzi, Mirza al-Qatari, Saleh Hassan, Ali Isa Ahmed and Hussain Howaida.
They were accused of possessing leaflets containing false news and unfounded statements.
Hours before their trial began, a car exploded in the capital Manama but a government official said it was accidental.
"Investigations showed the explosion was caused by a gas cylinder. There were no casualties or damage," he said.
Shi'ite Moslems have launched sporadic attacks in the island state since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
Four Asians died on Friday in an arson attack on a shop in Manama, raising the number of people killed to more than 30 since 1994. Officials said the blaze was premeditated.
Friday's attack was the latest in a series of fires this week in Bahrain, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
Seven Bangladeshi workers died in March 1996 when suspected arsonists set a restaurant ablaze on the small island of Sitra, linked with Manama by a three km (1.8 mile) causeway.
